rationale: The agent verified the user’s identity using full name and zip, matched to a single account, before accessing orders. It looked up orders read-only to identify the tablet and correctly provided the tracking number. When asked about refund/reorder for a lost-after-delivery item, the agent appropriately declined within policy and offered escalation if there was a delivery issue. For order changes, the agent explicitly requested confirmation before each action: canceled the pending charger order with a stated reason and processed the refund to the gift card; identified the boots order, obtained confirmation to cancel, then canceled the entire pending order (which also included the kettle) and accurately reported the refund; later correctly explained that reinstating the kettle after cancellation isn’t possible and offered to help reorder. For the sneakers, the agent identified the delivered order, sought confirmation, then submitted an item-level return and communicated next steps. All actions were performed on the authenticated user’s orders, with no unsupported claims or unconfirmed writes. Minor communication nit: it could have reiterated that canceling #W5481803 would cancel both items before confirmation, but it did clearly ask to cancel the entire order number, which satisfies the confirmation requirement.
